page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-8GB is a Cloud Native virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1258.0 and Passmark CPU scoring 8006.57, both placing in the average tier. However, multi-core performance is constrained, as reflected by a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 3106.23 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3948.0. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 398.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 40.7 GB/sec for larger blocks, though write bandwidth is weaker at 23.27 GB/sec.

Due to its shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage, this server represents a budget-oriented tier. It offers resource density suitable for non-critical workloads where continuous maximum CPU performance is not required. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, software compilation tasks, or small-scale development and testing environments that can tolerate shared resource contention.
